summary: Reconciled the Railway static-frontend trust boundary: the browser uses a narrow fixed-scenario public synthetic API without a secret, while reset, SMS/voice initiation, provider callbacks, and manual scheduler control retain distinct server-side authentication and public commands cannot authorize external effects.
decisions: Keep the approved Railway-only topology: public static `web`, public long-running Node.js/TypeScript `api`, and private Railway `Postgres` connected by `DATABASE_URL`.
Do not place a scenario or operator token in Vite code, variables, storage, source maps, runtime configuration, or generated clients. `VITE_API_BASE_URL` is the browser's only deployment value.
Replace global `FinalsScenarioToken` OpenAPI security with explicit operation-level public-demo, operator, provider-callback, and scheduler trust classes.
Make finals role projections, metrics, FHIR, priority evidence, readiness submission, work-item commands, and CareLink request/commands anonymous only for the controlled illustrative finals scenario.

Require `OperatorControlToken` using `X-OncoReady-Operator-Token` for deterministic reset and SMS/voice initiation. Store it as server-only `ONCOREADY_OPERATOR_TOKEN` and retire `ONCOREADY_SCENARIO_TOKEN` after migration.
Retain provider signature authentication on Twilio/ElevenLabs callbacks and opaque `CRON_SECRET` bearer authentication on the manual tick endpoint.
Set `ONCOREADY_PUBLIC_DEMO_ENABLED=false` by default; the controlled finals deployment explicitly opts in with `true` and fails closed otherwise.
Keep command `scenario_id` for event/idempotency consistency but constrain it in OpenAPI to `11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111` and reject any mismatch before domain execution.

Constrain public readiness to `channel: web`; signed callbacks are the only SMS/voice outcome boundary. Reduce public CareLink creation to `work_item_id` plus command context and derive every plan/provider/location field from server-owned finals state.
Treat `actor_role` as unverified demo provenance, not identity. Enforce an explicit route, aggregate/resource, action, current-state, and role-claim matrix server-side.
Give public mutations a hard database-only effect ceiling: they may append events/projections and internal workflow state but cannot create or authorize provider outbox work.

Accept provider dispatch authorization only from an operator-authenticated communication command; persist the authorization source and still apply fixed recipient/provider/script allowlists, kill switches, rate limits, versions, and idempotency.
Use exact CORS as browser isolation and configuration hygiene, never as authentication. Apply body limits and per-origin/IP/operation rate limits to public mutations.
Keep deterministic reset outside the public application. The operator invokes it by script/direct API before rehearsal, and it suppresses all external effects.
Keep the normal scheduler inside the API process with PostgreSQL time, advisory locking, bounded claims, leases, and reconcile-before-retry; the protected HTTP tick is manual/preflight only.
Complete ML, backend, frontend, Railway, contract-policy, and no-secret-bundle readiness with all external switches false before configuring or enabling Twilio and ElevenLabs.

Retain FULL testing and HIGH risk with a dedicated security review because public mutations, privileged reset/provider actions, signed callbacks, and real bounded communications cross material trust boundaries.

risks.description: A secret embedded in the Railway static frontend would be publicly recoverable and would provide no meaningful authorization.
risks.mitigation: Send no secret to the browser; use a narrow public synthetic API and keep operator/provider/scheduler credentials server-side.

risks.description: Anonymous commands could trigger cost, harassment, consent violations, or misleading provider success if they can create external work.
risks.mitigation: Enforce a database-only public effect ceiling and require operator-authenticated, fixed-target communication commands before any provider outbox authorization.

risks.description: The local role selector is not identity and cannot protect confidential or role-private data from anonymous callers.
risks.mitigation: Use illustrative data only, describe role as demo context, preserve server-minimized projection schemas, and require real identity before introducing protected data.

risks.description: Leaked operator, provider, or scheduler credentials could enable destructive reset, outbound communication, or privileged processing.
risks.mitigation: Keep credentials only in Railway server variables, use separate scopes, redact logs, rate-limit privileged routes, rotate on exposure, and keep provider switches false outside controlled windows.

risks.description: Anonymous visitors can vandalize or race the shared synthetic scenario even when they cannot cause external effects.
risks.mitigation: Use fixed scenario/action policies, versions, idempotency, bounded rate limits, one controlled environment, monitoring, and operator-authenticated deterministic reset.

risks.description: CORS may be mistaken for authentication or a forwarded client address may be trusted incorrectly for rate limiting.
risks.mitigation: Document CORS as defense-in-depth, enforce consequence limits independently, trust only Railway's known proxy hop, and test direct non-browser requests.

risks.description: Process restart or ambiguous provider acceptance can duplicate a consequential action.
risks.mitigation: Use durable PostgreSQL claims, committed provider attempts, stable identities, signed callbacks, and reconcile-before-retry; lease expiry alone never permits resend.

notes_for_next_agent: CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUIRED before frontend API integration: update `contracts/openapi.yaml` exactly as described in `docs/architecture/SYSTEM.md`; event contracts do not change.

Public operations: GET finals projection/metrics/FHIR/priority and POST readiness/work-item/CareLink request/CareLink commands, all with `security: []`, fixed finals scenario, explicit 403 policy errors, and 429 on mutations. Readiness is web-only; CareLink creation accepts no client-selected plan fields.
Operator operations: POST reset/SMS/voice with `OperatorControlToken` header `X-OncoReady-Operator-Token`; manual tick remains `CronSecret`; callbacks retain official signature headers.
Frontend must generate a client with no operator token parameter, use only public operations, and keep reset and provider-initiation controls out of the anonymous journey.
Backend must enforce public no-outbox authorization as an application/domain invariant, not only a router convention. CORS is not the authorization control.

Environment decisions: web=`VITE_API_BASE_URL`; api=`ONCOREADY_PUBLIC_DEMO_ENABLED`, server-only `ONCOREADY_OPERATOR_TOKEN`, `DATABASE_URL`, exact origins, `CRON_SECRET`, scheduler settings, and provider variables/switches.
Keep `EXTERNAL_ACTIONS_ENABLED=false`, `TWILIO_SMS_ENABLED=false`, and `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_ENABLED=false` through ML/backend/frontend/Railway readiness. Provider setup and live proof are a later phase.
Scheduler decision is unchanged: one long-running API owns the poller; PostgreSQL owns durable due work/claims; protected tick is manual/preflight only.
FastAPI remains human-permitted but is not selected for this slice because the existing TypeScript implementation and contracts make a rewrite unnecessary risk.

FULL independent testing must include direct non-browser calls, arbitrary scenario/action rejection, no-secret bundle inspection, public no-external-effect proof, operator auth, callbacks, scheduler overlap, and the complete browser journey.
